release.note: Settled by the new tolerance. Post's tol va vb K is now errAt (prodV va vb K) (steps K), the DotE5m2 fact at K = 64 applied step by step against the exact partial sums (E(t+1) = (1 + rho)*E t + rho*(|S t| + B t) + alpha, E 0 = 0), which acc_step closes with err_step and which never exceeds the old bound (tol_le_tolA). Since Post holds for every input, the all-zero kernel, a skipped loop and any skipped K-step now break it at every covered K, 2817 <= K <= 4096 included: MatmulE5m2.Reject proves zero_rejected (one product 1 in the last step, tol <= rho + 200*alpha by tol_spike, room in float16) and drop_rejected (the same input for the last step; 1 at 64s and -1 at 64s + 64 against a column of 1s for an earlier step, tol below 1/5). I read the module in full and checked the statements with full names: they speak of OutSpec's own float16 clause, on finite float8e5 inputs that Pre allows. The same spike input also rejects S/2 and -S at every K (work/Round2.lean checks S/2 at K = 4096) and a float8e5 rounding of 1.5625. errAt is the bound the per-step fact gives with |acc| <= |S_t| + E_t, so no tighter statement follows from the library's DotE5m2; what it still admits on dense inputs (72.8% on all-ones, about 2.3*|S| on randn data at K = 4096, by my own evaluation of errAt) is the library's allowed device error, which L119 leaves to a later library round, and the README states it. Keeping K <= 4096 is then right for the host's use.

Settled: the README's Specification is rewritten for the new tolerance. It no longer says that -S or a read of another row passes from K = 2817, it lists S/2 and -S among what the spike input rejects at every covered K, and 'What it does not reject' gives the bound on the input at hand with figures I re-evaluated (13.3% and 170.8% for one product in step 0, 7.3% and 72.8% on one-sign products, about 7 and 114 on randn data at K = 512 and 4096, 0.124 for the pair input at s = 0, K = 4096, and the spike bound below 0.026 for 1.5625).

notes: Round 2: I read every changed Lean file in full (Defs.lean, Basic.lean, Program.lean, the new Reject.lean, the root module): no notation, instance, open renaming, option or look-alike name, and every new name (prodV, partSum, partMag, stepMag, errAt, tol, tolA, stepSum, spikeP, pairP, the float8e5 inputs one8, mone8, zero8 and their rows) is a kernel definition I read; #print axioms of main, consistent, satisfiable, zero_rejected and drop_rejected shows only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound (work/Round2.lean). The model, map, conditions and assumption digests are those of round 1. Small remark, non-blocking: the docstring of the Inst.ok field K_le changed (it now cites the rejection lemmas) while the conditions digest stayed the same, since an item's digest holds its roots' docstrings and not those of the kernel's other constants, such as a structure's field projections; the new text is accurate, so nothing is needed here.
